The concept of sovereignty was articulated by Carl Schmitt as he who decides on the exception. A proper society attempts to set and uphold specific standard normative procedures. When order persists in a civilization and everything is operating as intended, then there shouldn't be a need for any decision that would require discretion. For example, the legal system only exists to deal with citizens who decide to act in a way that violates the norms of society. If norms were not violated, then there wouldn't be any need for a legal system at all. As Schmitt explains, nobody actually has the omnipotence to account for what these exceptions may be. Otherwise, you could just codify them within the legal order. A true exception is definitionally impossible to predict and define. Because you can't account for everything, you have to allocate somebody or something to independently deal with these exceptions as they come, not preemptively. When something happens that does fall outside of the already defined bounds of society, the entity or person that is entrusted with discretionary authority to deal with it is the truly sovereign force of that system. Our buildings may be ugly and soulless but we can still build them. But this only proves that our technical and spiritual health are in fact not entirely reliant on each other. The native populations of Europe and the nations which are derived from them are all high IQ. We are experts at composing systems. And no matter what, if our population is preserved, we will always be able to sustain a society from a technical sense. Whether this involves the construction and maintenance of our roads or our political systems more generally, the operative functions of society will persist. But especially with this being a given, the true determination of our societal greatness then becomes entirely predicated on where we are drawing our inspiration from. And we are continuing to draw all of our inspiration from rotten materialistic ideologies. And it is costing us our nation's soul.

And while that denigration may be easily viewed through our architecture, this problem goes far beyond it. Our societal designers, from our architects all the way to our political theorists, are not producing the intellectual ammunition needed for our technicians, all the way from our real estate developers to those who hold political office. True, deep-seated change will depend on the inspiration.
